channel.title: America After Dark with Dudley Duke
channel.description: Three unhurried hours of overnight talk radio, weeknights midnight to 3 AM Eastern from DeLand, Florida. Dudley Duke opens with the real news of the night — state, national and international — then the phones open to callers from across America and around the world. Every night closes with Radio Graffiti, where each caller gets one line, and one line only. Listen live at americaafterdarkradio.com.
channel.itunes:author: Dudley Duke

item.title: Wednesday Night, November 25, 2026
item.description: The Wednesday night show, aired Thursday, November 26, 2026, 12:00–3:00 AM Eastern from DeLand, Florida. The night's real news: the Army's controlled detonation of 68 barrels of crystallized lead azide at Middletown, Iowa goes off in two blasts Wednesday morning, with EPA monitors reading zero airborne lead and the town's all-clear before evening; Tennessee tech support worker Victoria Broderick beats eight-term Representative Scott DesJarlais by about 360 votes; a federal jury awards six million dollars to a former Wyoming Boys' School resident, and the school announces it is ending detention rooms; Alaska Senator Dan Sullivan concedes to Mary Peltola; the White House proposes new tariffs on 14 trading partners, China included; a federal judge blocks the birthright-citizenship order and another blocks the FCC's early review of ABC's licenses; GDP grew 4.3 percent in the third quarter while inflation ran 3.8 percent in October; the CDC counts nine measles deaths and 6,039 cases, a 35-year high; the Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade is postponed for the first time ever, to Saturday; Kilmar Ábrego García lands in Madrid after leaving the United States voluntarily; the first death anywhere linked to bird flu in dairy cattle, in Yakima County, Washington; Iran claims tankers hit mines in the Strait of Hormuz, unverified, and the Houthis say they struck Saudi Arabia's Ras Tanura refinery, also unconfirmed; Russian strikes cut power in five Ukrainian regions and Ukraine says it hit a Russian air base and two refineries; an Islamic State attack kills two in Hasaka, Syria, and a Saudi national is kidnapped in Niger; Israel kills a second senior Hamas security official in 24 hours; and RSF drones kill 19 civilians in Sudan. Plus callers from across America and around the world, and Radio Graffiti to close.

item.title: Tuesday Night, November 24, 2026
item.description: The Tuesday night show, aired Wednesday, November 25, 2026, 12:00–3:00 AM Eastern from DeLand, Florida. The night's real news: the Army's controlled detonation of more than 9,700 pounds of crystallized lead azide at Middletown, Iowa, is set for Wednesday morning, with the town evacuated and a five-mile cone, after the Eighth Circuit cleared it; California Governor Newsom's plan to commute all 548 death sentences is before the state Supreme Court, with victims' families and 28 district attorneys suing to stop it, and President Trump calls it one of the most shocking acts of injustice at the Justice Department; New York Governor Hochul signs a five-year ban on AI chatbot toys, effective February 2027, after a robot suggested a child jump out a window; Wisconsin records a third measles death, with 920 cases in 2026 and the 14th measles death in the country this year; Virginia and Oregon sue SpaceX over Grok's "spicy mode"; the United States blacklists Singapore chip firm Megaspeed over suspected Nvidia chip diversion to China; Iran's Revolutionary Guard claims three tankers hit mines in the Strait of Hormuz, unverified, with traffic 65 percent below pre-war levels, and a Houthi drone hits a tower in Riyadh; North Korea expels the head of Switzerland's Pyongyang diplomatic office; about 450 German schools get identical emailed bomb threats, ruled hoaxes; and Russia warns Estonia its actions are on the verge of triggering open war as Estonia closes its land border December 1. Plus callers from across America and around the world, and Radio Graffiti to close.

item.title: Monday Night, November 23, 2026
item.description: The Monday night show, aired Tuesday, November 24, 2026, 12:00–3:00 AM Eastern from DeLand, Florida. The night's real news: Ohio's Freedom to Carry Act reaches Governor DeWine's desk, lowering the carry age to 18 and barring cities from restricting guns; New York Governor Hochul vetoes a bill requiring accuracy warnings on artificial intelligence; Oregon lays out a universal health plan with no premiums or deductibles; New Jersey Governor Sherrill signs an executive order overhauling reading instruction; Nvidia reinstates Jensen Huang as chief executive eleven days after his resignation; the Second Circuit gives President Trump a new path to move his hush money case to federal court; Representative Jimmy Gomez resigns after the Ethics Committee finds substantial evidence of sexual misconduct; Democrats clinch at least 258 House seats, their largest majority since 1992; the COP31 climate summit collapses in Antalya; Ukraine sinks the Russian corvette Merkury off Libya with sea drones; the United States sanctions dozens tied to Iran shadow banking; and Spain's Supreme Court clears Carles Puigdemont to return from exile. Plus callers from across America and around the world, and Radio Graffiti to close.

item.title: Friday Night, November 20, 2026
item.description: The Friday night show, aired Saturday, November 21, 2026, 12:00–3:00 AM Eastern from DeLand, Florida. The night's real news: Washington fines the Longview paper mill $10.1 million after the May explosion that killed 11 workers; New York Governor Hochul vetoes a food-safety bill that would have banned Red 3, potassium bromate and propylparaben; Texas Governor-elect Hinojosa promises a statewide vote on legalizing marijuana and says he will rescind the hemp THC order; Indiana's Medicaid work requirements take effect January 1, with about 58,000 people estimated out of compliance; the Nasdaq falls 5.28 percent in a brutal week for tech stocks, its worst since March 2020, with Nvidia down 14 percent; President Trump holds a 90-minute press conference, threatening a tax on data centers and talking deals with Democrats; Congress faces a December 11 shutdown deadline as the White House demands $350 billion for the Pentagon; a second federal judge blocks the president's triumphal arch, calling it a rushed job; Russia launches a massive missile and drone barrage on Ukraine hours after the Shenzhen summit, with debris spilling into Poland; Iran signals openness to a deal as a tanker is struck in the Strait of Hormuz and four oil trustees are sanctioned; Britain and the European Union hold a Brexit reset summit with 100,000 youth mobility places for ages 18 to 31; and Myanmar rejects the World Court's genocide ruling, 9 to 6. Plus callers from across America and around the world, and Radio Graffiti to close.

item.title: Thursday Night, November 19, 2026
item.description: The Thursday night show, aired Friday, November 20, 2026, 12:00–3:00 AM Eastern from DeLand, Florida. The night's real news: the Army postpones its lead-azide detonation in Iowa to Monday, November 23, after a day of outrage over a possible 100-mile toxic plume; Alabama state Rep. Patrick Sellers is indicted on four federal wire-fraud counts over more than $240,000 in COVID relief; North Carolina's lame-duck legislature sends a $186 million budget bill to Gov. Stein; Gov. DeSantis urges lawmakers to strip Florida cities of the power to raise fees after Amendment 3; the Senate rejects the Iran war-powers resolution, 48–51; Anthropic makes the biggest IPO in history, raising $81 billion and closing up 17%; the Senate passes a sweeping bipartisan energy permitting bill, 62–33; President Trump posthumously pardons Pete Rose for his 1990 tax convictions, though it changes nothing for the Hall of Fame; Trump, Xi and Putin hold the first-ever trilateral summit in Shenzhen; Trump defers any decision on renewed Iran strikes into next year; Ukraine strikes the Crimean Bridge for a third time in a week as Europe's Coalition of the Willing meets in Berlin; and the World Court rules Myanmar committed genocide against the Rohingya, the first state ever held accountable for genocide in the court's 80-year history. Plus callers from across America and around the world, and Radio Graffiti to close.

item.title: Wednesday Night, November 18, 2026
item.description: The Wednesday night show, aired Thursday, November 19, 2026, 12:00–3:00 AM Eastern from DeLand, Florida. The night's real news: New York Governor Hochul unveils a nuclear master plan calling for 5 gigawatts of new reactors; Texas launches the first-ever statewide audit of a U.S. Senate race, hand-checking ballots in the Talarico–Paxton contest; eight Black women Democrats now hold statewide office in Georgia, led by Keisha Lance Bottoms, the nation's first Black woman governor-elect; Virginia Governor Spanberger unveils a housing package built on transit zones, surplus state land and a preservation fund; top security officials tell Congress the week's outages were not an attack, while Iran keeps probing U.S. infrastructure; Nvidia posts record earnings of $115.8 billion as its board rejects Jensen Huang's return and Congress sets December testimony; House Democrats nominate Hakeem Jeffries for speaker, 251–11; Iran widens the Gulf war, hitting a U.S.-hosted air base in Kuwait and sites in Bahrain after U.S. jets strike Qeshm Island; Xi and Putin meet in Shenzhen as President Trump arrives for Thursday's first-ever trilateral summit; the European Union proposes a €45 billion loan to Ukraine for 2027, repayable only once Russia pays reparations; Israel's Knesset elects Matan Kahana speaker, 66–52, in a win for the bloc opposed to Netanyahu. Plus callers from across America and around the world, and Radio Graffiti to close.

item.title: Tuesday Night, November 17, 2026
item.description: The Tuesday night show, aired Wednesday, November 18, 2026, 12:00–3:00 AM Eastern from DeLand, Florida. The night's real news: Indiana's Chris Garten is seated and elected Senate president pro tempore after the state Supreme Court lifts the bar on his oath, and he asks for a recount of his own race, which he leads by fewer than 300 votes; California prosecutors ask the state Supreme Court to block Governor Newsom's plan to commute all 548 death sentences; the Memphis schools state takeover board meets for the first time in five months, still blocked by a judge; New Hampshire's new Democratic supermajorities plan a school-funding overhaul as voters' tax caps complicate the math; the United States loses its measles elimination status after 26 years, with 5,412 cases in 2026, the most since 1991; the Transportation Department formally asks Congress for $50.1 billion to fix air traffic control after Friday's ground stop, as Senate Democrats demand answers and the FAA halts Juniper router installs; Paris Hilton and Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez press the House for a vote on the DEFIANCE Act against nonconsensual deepfakes; the Senate clears a second hurdle for the bipartisan permitting-reform bill, 70–27, with a final vote possible this week; Iran fires drones at a U.S. radar facility in Bahrain, its third strike in days; Ukraine destroys a section of the Crimean Bridge as Russia hits two of Kyiv's bridges; President Trump heads to Asia for a first-ever three-way summit with Xi and Putin in Shenzhen; Japan scrambles fighter jets after suspected Russian aircraft breach its airspace. Plus callers from across America and around the world, and Radio Graffiti to close.

item.title: Monday Night, November 16, 2026
item.description: The Monday night show, aired Tuesday, November 17, 2026, 12:00–3:00 AM Eastern from DeLand, Florida. The night's real news: Alaska's Senate count sits 52 votes short of a majority with more ballots to count Tuesday; Scott Colom's historic win in Mississippi stands, the first Black senator from the state since Reconstruction; the California coast takes its biggest swell in a decade, with 50- to 60-foot waves at Mavericks; air travel comes back after Friday's nationwide ground stop, with more than 18,000 flights cancelled through the weekend; the United States is set to lose its measles elimination status after 26 years; President Trump departs for Asia and a first-ever three-way summit with Xi and Putin; SpaceX catches a Starship returning from orbit, a first; tankers are hit in and around the Strait of Hormuz; Ukraine talks hold out the largest prisoner exchange of the war, with Europe to get a seat; the United States condemns Iranian drone strikes in Bahrain as a third carrier strike group arrives in the region; record migrant arrivals overwhelm Spain's Canary Islands. Plus callers from across America and around the world, and Radio Graffiti to close.

item.title: Friday Night, November 13, 2026
item.description: The Friday night show, aired Saturday, November 14, 2026, 12:00–3:00 AM Eastern from DeLand, Florida. The night's real news: the FAA orders a nationwide ground stop after a telecommunications outage, the third in American aviation history, with more than 10,000 flights delayed and more than 3,000 cancelled; Jonathan Kreiss-Tomkins wins Alaska's governor's race at 37, the youngest in state history and the first Democrat since 2002; Kansas governor-elect Cindy Holscher lays out her priorities at her first press conference after winning by 7,644 votes; Indigenous women post historic midterm wins in New Mexico, Arizona, Minnesota and the Navajo Nation; a tanker loses steering and collides with a docked riverboat in New Orleans, 32 hospitalized, all 197 aboard accounted for; Europe joins the next round of Ukraine talks, with the largest prisoner exchange of the war in prospect; SpaceX Starship Flight 15 reaches orbit and deploys 26 satellites while the booster is lost; Jake Bauers signs a four-year, $58 million deal with the Boston Red Sox; a Microsoft 365 outage is mostly restored; measles cases pass 5,000 as the U.S. nears losing elimination status. Plus callers from across America and around the world, and Radio Graffiti to close.

item.title: Thursday Night, November 12, 2026
item.description: The Thursday night show, aired Friday, November 13, 2026, 12:00–3:00 AM Eastern from DeLand, Florida. The night's real news: Cindy Holscher wins the Kansas governor's race by 7,358 votes, the closest in the state since 1974; a building collapse in Brooklyn kills eight, including two children; Mary Peltola leads Dan Sullivan by about 4,000 votes in Alaska's uncalled Senate race; Nvidia founder Jensen Huang resigns as chief executive, with Colette Kress named interim CEO and shares falling; President Trump says the U.S. does not need a deal with Iran and directs Vice President Vance to focus on fraud in Democratic-run cities; U.S. envoys meet Vladimir Putin in Moscow and fly to Dublin to brief Volodymyr Zelensky, with Europe joining the next round of talks and the largest prisoner exchange of the war in prospect; Defense Secretary Hegseth awards a medal to the sentinel who corrected his group at the Tomb of the Unknown Soldier; the president threatens to double tariffs on Mexico; consumer prices rise 0.4 percent in October; the House passes the Major Richard Star Act 392–18. Plus callers from across America and around the world, and Radio Graffiti to close.

item.title: Wednesday Night, November 11, 2026
item.description: The Wednesday night show, aired Thursday, November 12, 2026, 12:00–3:00 AM Eastern from DeLand, Florida. The night's real news: Texas lawmakers file to repeal the data-center sales-tax exemption, a break projected to cost $3.3 billion; Ohio's incoming governor Amy Acton faces a bid to weaken her veto; California governor-elect Xavier Becerra promises cooperation as Medi-Cal coverage for more than a million people sits at risk; House Republicans elect Jim Jordan minority leader; the USDA proposes a food-stamp rule that would cut benefits for 6.3 million people; the U.S. is poised to lose its measles elimination status; Ukraine and Russia agree a major prisoner release in U.S.-led talks in Abu Dhabi; hoax bomb threats empty schools across Italy; Israel's new Knesset is sworn in with no government and a December 6 deadline. Plus callers from across America and around the world, and Radio Graffiti to close.

item.title: Tuesday Night, November 10, 2026
item.description: The Tuesday night show, aired Wednesday, November 11, 2026, 12:00–3:00 AM Eastern from DeLand, Florida. The night's real news: California voters reject a proposed billionaire tax; the Mississippi and Alaska Senate races still uncalled; Governor Katie Hobbs reelected in Arizona; the Hegseth–Massie impeachment clash; the U.S. skips the UN human rights review for a second year; Senate Judiciary's lame-duck judge push advances a nominee 16–6; tanker strikes in the Strait of Hormuz with crude at two-month lows; an investigation in Guinea-Bissau involving rapper Vigario Luis Balanta; a fog pile-up in Bulgaria kills at least ten. Plus callers from across America and around the world, and Radio Graffiti to close.

item.title: Monday Night, November 9, 2026
item.description: The Monday night show, aired Tuesday, November 10, 2026, 12:00–3:00 AM Eastern from DeLand, Florida. The night's real news: Keisha Lance Bottoms elected governor of Georgia — the first Black woman ever elected governor of any state; the Mississippi and Alaska Senate races still uncounted; Eric Armstrong wins an Iowa House seat after suspending his campaign; Amish Shah wins Arizona's open 1st District; the Justice Department drops its California ballot case; Ukraine talks open in Abu Dhabi; Pope Leo XIV draws 2.5 million to Mass in Buenos Aires; the Strait of Hormuz severely restricted. Plus callers from across America and around the world, and Radio Graffiti to close.

item.title: Sunday Night, November 8, 2026
item.description: The Sunday night show, aired Monday, November 9, 2026, 12:00–3:00 AM Eastern from DeLand, Florida. The night's real news: Alaska's Senate race sits 637 votes apart with three quarters counted; Democrats sweep Texas statewide; Colorado voters approve public-lands funding; Amy Acton is Ohio's governor-elect; a deadly shooting in Krakow, Poland; strikes in the Strait of Hormuz; Paraguay's former president charged and detained; Pope Leo XIV on the Uruguay-Argentina border. Plus callers from across America and around the world, and Radio Graffiti to close.

item.title: Saturday Night, November 7, 2026
item.description: The Saturday night show, aired Sunday, November 8, 2026, 12:00–3:00 AM Eastern from DeLand, Florida. The night's real news: Keisha Lance Bottoms elected Georgia's first woman governor and the first Black woman elected governor of a U.S. state; Chris Pappas becomes the first openly gay man elected to the U.S. Senate; the Justice Department drops its California ballot suit; Pope Leo XIV celebrates Mass before 40,000 in Paysandu, Uruguay; airstrikes near Sanaa kill at least 27 in Yemen. Plus callers from across America and Radio Graffiti to close.

item.title: Friday Night, November 6, 2026
item.description: The Friday night show, aired Saturday, November 7, 2026, 12:00–3:00 AM Eastern from DeLand, Florida. The night's real news: California commutes all 548 death sentences; Gina Hinojosa wins the Texas governor's race; the October jobs report beats forecasts; Paraguay's president removed after a bank collapse; Paul Mackenzie sentenced to 200 years in Kenya; Pope Leo XIV begins a 12-day South America tour. Plus callers from across America and Radio Graffiti to close.

item.title: Thursday Night, November 5, 2026
item.description: The Thursday night show, aired Friday, November 6, 2026, 12:00–3:00 AM Eastern from DeLand, Florida. Three hours of real State, National and International news, callers from across America and around the world, and Radio Graffiti in the final half hour.

item.title: Wednesday Night, November 4, 2026 — The Premiere
item.description: The premiere of America After Dark, aired Thursday, November 5, 2026, 12:00–3:00 AM Eastern. The night's news, all researched from real reporting: Florida's Amendment 3 property-tax fight and the planned special session; Democrats taking control of Congress in the midterm elections; and the aftermath of the deadly high-speed rail crash in Spain. Plus listener calls through the night and Radio Graffiti in the final half hour — one line per caller.
